description:
🔥 Pakistan Smog & Satellite Hotspots (MODIS & VIIRS)

Tackling Pakistan’s smog crisis by building an AI web app to harmonize 20+ years of satellite fire data (Punjab & Sindh), flag abnormal weeks, and generate plain-language insights.

💻 Me: AI/LLM pipelines, RAG, Full-Stack Web Dev.

My portfolio: Rehan Sathio

🤝 Looking for:

• Earth Science / GIS / Remote Sensing

• Data Analysis & Stats

• UI/UX & Pitch Storytelling

(Curious beginners welcome! In-person @ Karachi)
summary: Aatish (Urdu for "fire") turns 26 years of NASA satellite fire detections over Pakistan into one consistent record. MODIS (Terra and Aqua, since 2000) has the long history, but its successor VIIRS (Suomi NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21) sees about 4× more hotspots by day and 15× more at night. Simply adding the two makes fires look as if they jumped 6.9× in 2012, when only the satellites changed. We weight every VIIRS detection by the measured chance that MODIS would also have seen it, by fire power, day or night, month and location. The result is one MODIS-equivalent monthly series from November 2000 to 13 November 2026. On years held out of the fit, it reproduces monthly totals with a 9.5% median error (R² 0.957). The web app lets anyone pick a province or draw an area, see a years × months burning calendar, compare this month with the same days in every past year, read an 80% uncertainty band and a 1–3 month outlook, ask questions in English or Urdu, and download the hotspots as CSV. In Pakistan, where crop-residue burning peaks after the wheat and rice harvests, it answers one question with evidence: is this season unusual?
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Aatish is a harmonized fire-hotspot calendar for Pakistan. It merges every MODIS and VIIRS active-fire detection that NASA FIRMS recorded over the country from November 2000 to 13 November 2026 (1,886,811 detections from 5 satellites) into one monthly series in a single unit, "MODIS-equivalent hotspots". The sensor of origin no longer matters, so the charts show changes in burning, not changes in satellites.

In the web app a user can:

- pick a province, draw a polygon or box, or type a point and radius;

- choose any date range and see a years × months burning calendar on a colour-blind-safe ramp, with the value of every cell on hover;

- see whether the current month is unusual: the partial month is compared with the same days in every earlier year, giving a ratio, a percentile, a rank and an 80% uncertainty band;

- see key figures for the area: total, peak month, highest year (worded "among the highest" when the gap is inside the band) and the long-term trend (claimed only when significant and larger than the band);

- read a 1–3 month outlook with its tested skill and range;

- watch every month play on a full-screen map: density heat, individual hotspots with time, satellite and fire power, a province anomaly map, and NASA GIBS true-colour imagery for a chosen day;

- download the hotspots in the area as CSV (with their harmonization weights), the monthly table as CSV and the calendar as PNG, or share a link that restores the exact view;

- ask questions in plain English or Urdu ("Is this November worse than usual in Lahore?"). The assistant only answers with numbers it looked up in our data.

HOW IT WORKS (the science)

1. Clean every stream the same way: MODIS confidence ≥ 30, VIIRS nominal or high. One location mask (1,443 cells at 0.01°) removes brick kilns, gas flares and other static heat sources from every sensor and year, including near-real-time data, which has no "type" field. Satellite outages are marked as no data, not as zero fires.

2. Weight every VIIRS detection. From 2012–2022, when both instruments flew with stable orbits, we measured the probability that Aqua MODIS also detected a fire that Suomi NPP saw (within 1.5 km, same day), by fire radiative power and day or night. It rises from about 1% for the weakest fires to 32% by day and 54% by night for the strongest. A month-of-year factor, a local 1° correction shrunk toward 1, and a per-satellite factor complete the weight. The series uses the mean of whichever VIIRS satellites were active, so one satellite's outage does not create a dip. Weights add up, so any drawn area gets a consistent total.

3. Stitch three eras: Terra alone, scaled to Terra + Aqua, until July 2002; MODIS observed until September 2022; VIIRS-derived values from October 2022, when MODIS orbital drift starts to change what it detects. The October–December 2022 hand-off ratios are 0.94, 1.01 and 1.06.

4. Put a band on every number: each derived month carries an 80% band from held-out years, sized by its count.

VALIDATION (leave-one-year-out, 2012–2022)

- Pakistan monthly totals: 9.5% median absolute error, R² 0.957.

- 1° grid cells: 17.1% median error, R² 0.943.

- Applying the S-NPP fit to NOAA-20: +1.5% bias.

- Anomaly correlation 0.855. Terra vs Aqua, two copies of the same MODIS instrument, only reach 0.875, so we are close to the noise floor.

- The real 2011→2012 change is ×1.48, not the ×6.9 seen in raw counts. Over 2002–2025 Pakistan's fire activity rose about 2.7% a year, which is statistically significant.

- Forecast: one month ahead it is 7.8% more accurate than the 10-year typical value (rolling test 2016–2026). Beyond 3 months the app only shows the typical range and says it is not a forecast.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Every autumn, smoke from crop-residue burning adds to the winter smog over Lahore and the rest of Punjab. Without a consistent record nobody can say whether this season is worse than usual, because the satellite record itself changes scale. With Aatish, a journalist, land manager, researcher or emergency responder can check any area in seconds. For example, Punjab's 1–13 November 2026 is 2.10× the usual for those days (820 vs 391, higher than 89% of past Novembers, provisional data). They can then download the hotspots behind that answer. When MODIS retires, the record continues on the same scale.

TOOLS

- Data: NASA FIRMS (MODIS C6.1, VIIRS 375 m S-NPP / NOAA-20 / NOAA-21), standard and near-real-time; FIRMS area API for 2026; NASA GIBS imagery.

- Pipeline: Python, pandas, NumPy, SciPy, DuckDB, Parquet. Deterministic build (~30 s) and a validation script that fails on any regression.

- API: FastAPI + DuckDB over a 47 MB Parquet file, about 40–50 ms per area query.

- Web: Next.js, React, TypeScript, MapLibre GL, ECharts, three.js (3D calendar), Tailwind CSS. Works offline in "Archive Mode" from a pre-computed bundle if the API is down.

- Assistant: Google Gemini with function calling over read-only tools.

WHAT IS CREATIVE

- One additive weight per detection instead of a regression on totals. Any shape anyone draws is harmonized automatically, and the weight has a physical meaning.

- The "sensor illusion" toggle on the home page shows the fake 2012 jump in raw counts, then the harmonized trend.

- Honesty rules are built into the wording: no "record year" or "trend" unless the gap beats the uncertainty band, and every near-real-time number is labelled provisional.

- A bilingual (English/Urdu) assistant that cannot make up numbers.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

- Detections are not fires and not burned area; the app says so.

- Near-real-time data is provisional and is labelled as such.

- Coverage is Pakistan only. The method is general, but the weights are fitted to this region, and bands for very small drawn areas are an extrapolation.

- Accessibility: colour-blind-safe ramps, numbers on hover, keyboard controls, 390 px mobile layout.

- Jammu & Kashmir is shown as disputed territory on the map.

- Event rule: all data was downloaded and processed after the event start (14 Nov 2026, 09:00 PKT).
